objective: Catch subtle errors in diagnosing a wrong RAG answer.

sources.title: Es et al. 2023, Ragas: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation

followUp.question: Describe a case where retrieval and generation both contribute to one bad answer.
rubric: fix ranking and prompt evidence order

transfer.scenario: A model upgrade is proposed after users complain about wrong answers. You have one day. What evidence do you collect before agreeing?
rubric: classify retrieval vs generation vs freshness
run test set on both models

narration.text: A user asked about parental leave and got the old twelve-week figure instead of the new sixteen.
First, I pull the logs to see which chunks were retrieved for that question.
The chunks are from the old handbook, so this is a retrieval and freshness problem, not a generation one.
The answer matched those chunks closely, so our faithfulness score for it was high.
A high faithfulness score tells us the answer was correct, so our evaluation worked as intended.
The fix is to upgrade to a larger model, which will know that the leave policy changed.
We'll also remove superseded chunks and filter retrieval to the current policy versions.
Then we'll add this question to the test set, so it's checked on every change.

planted.misconception: High faithfulness means the answer is correct.
planted.whyWrong: Faithfulness measures whether claims are supported by the retrieved context. Here the context was stale, so a faithful answer was wrong. The evaluation missed it because it lacked a correctness check against current expected answers and freshness cases.
acceptableCorrections: Faithfulness only shows the answer matched the retrieved text; we also need correctness checks against current answers.
Our evaluation missed this because it had no freshness or correctness cases.

explain: faithfulness is support by context|groundedness|supported by retrieved|matches retrieved chunks|grounded in sources
stale context: faithful but wrong|faithful to stale chunks|outdated source
correct: add correctness against expected answers|expected answers|reference answers|ground truth|gold answers

planted.misconception: A bigger model fixes a retrieval or freshness failure.
planted.whyWrong: The model answered from the stale chunks it was given. A larger model still receives the same stale evidence; its training data won't reliably contain your internal policy change.
acceptableCorrections: A bigger model won't help; it gets the same stale chunks. Fix the index and the version filtering.
The fix is in ingestion and retrieval, not the model.
planted.exceptions: If the logs had shown the current chunk was retrieved and ignored, a model or prompt change could be a fix.

explain: model can't use evidence it never received|receives same stale evidence|retrieval problem
internal changes not in training data|not trained
correct: fix sync|remove superseded chunks|re-sync index|update index
